texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules. The acc used is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Guru Masala Stall, from where the food article, that is, 'Lal Mirch Powder' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 29.01.2011, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) A. K. Singh and Field Assistant (FA) J. S. Bisht under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. R. K. Sharma reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Guru Masala Stall at Stall No.1, Mirch Masala Market, Pul Bangash, Azad Market, Delhi - 110006, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Lal Mirch Powder which was being sold in loose condition, from the vendor to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. In Re vs Guru @ Gurusaran on 7 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40250656/ 1 Vide report dated 17.02.2011, the PA found the sample to be conforming to the standards. However, as the food article was being sold in loose and unpacked condition in violation of Clause 24 of Rule 49 of PFA Rules, investigation was conducted. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 24.03.2011 alleging violation of section 7(v) of PFA Act, as punishable section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 24.03.2011. 4. Based on the contents of the complaint, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against the accused on 20.09.2011 for commission of the offence punishable under section 16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 7(v) of PFA Act, read with Rule 49 (24) of PFA Rules, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. At the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 FI A. K. Singh, PW-2 Sh. R. K. Sharma (SDM/LHA) and PW-3 FA J. S. Bisht were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 29.01.2011 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gram of Lal Mirch Powder that was being sold in open and loosed condition, dividing it in three parts, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW- 1/A, Notice Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, Raid Report Ex.PW-1/D, Statement of accused Ex. PW1/E, PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/F and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/G. PA report Ex. PW-1/H was received and investigation was conducted by PW-1 who sent letters Ex. PW-1/I to Ex. PW-1/M to various authorities and accused. He received reply of the accused Ex. PW-1/N. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW- 1/O was taken from the Director PFA and thereafter, complaint Ex. PW- 1/P was filed in the court. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex. PW-1/Q was sent to the accused through post. PW-1 and PW-2 were duly cross - examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the accused had been falsely implicated or that the accused was packing the Mirch Powder in packets. PW-3 was however not cross- examined by the accused despite opportunity. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 24.02.2016 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Though he admitted the proceedings dated 29.01.2011, yet he claimed that the sample was not in open condition and was in a sealed packet of one kg. He chose not to lead evidence in defence.
texts.arguments: 7. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt as all the witnesses have supported its case and no material contradiction can be seen in their testimonies. In Re vs Guru @ Gurusaran on 7 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40250656/ 2 8. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has argued that no case is made out against the accused. The sole ground urged by the defence is that no public witness was joined in the proceeding to corroborate the version of the official witnesses. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.
